<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
          <jats:sec>
            <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
            <jats:p>It was reported that elevation of the intracellular concentration of free Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> ([Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]i) by a calcium ionophore increased the release of herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). Freely diffusible hydrogen peroxide (H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>) is implied to alter Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> homeostasis, which further enhances abnormal cellular activity, causing changes in signal transduction, and cellular dysfunction. Whether H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> could affect [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]i in HSV-1-infected cells had not been investigated.</jats:p>
          </jats:sec>
          <jats:sec>
            <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
            <jats:p>H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> treatment increased the amount of cell-free virus and decreased the proportion of viable cells. After the treatment, an elevation in [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]i was observed and the increase in [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]i was suppressed when intracellular and cytosolic Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> were buffered by Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> chelators. In the presence of Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> chelators, H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>-mediated increases of cell-free virus and cell death were also diminished. Electron microscopic analysis revealed enlarged cell junctions and a focal disintegration of the plasma membrane in H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>-treated cells.</jats:p>
          </jats:sec>
          <jats:sec>
            <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
            <jats:p>These results indicate that H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> can elevate [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]i and induces non-apoptotic cell death with membrane lesions, which is responsible for the increased release of HSV-1 from epithelial cells.</jats:p>
          </jats:sec>
title: Involvement of intracellular free Ca2+ in enhanced release of herpes simplex virus by hydrogen peroxide
